title: How stride piano was copied from bands
summary: Wooding says players like Ralph Rawson and Duke taught him stride, which imitates the bass, alto horn and melody parts of a marching band.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: So, we'd play at these parties. Well, each time we'd meet other fellows playing at the parties, and we learned how to, what you call, swing. There was a guy -- or, stride. There was a guy there that -- for -- a fellow named Rawson, Ralph Rawson. He came over from New York, and he -- and there was another fellow there we'd call Duke something -- this fellow could take "Onward Christian Soldiers", and really swing it. What we called swing today, but stride, but stride, and I'll tell you about this stride business which a lot of people don't know. We got stride from watching, listening to bands. You see, the bass, when he goes down, it was the bass and the trombones, things like that. When he came up, he was alto horn. Like when you say, "oom-pa, oom-pa, oom-pa, oom-pa,". Now, and then the right hand, well, there was a left hand in the bass clef, and the right hand was always, it took off the trumpets or the clarinets, or one of those things. So, we found out from the older piano players, that this was the way a band would play. We would play the same thing on a piano, that's that stride piano. We'd play all such things like Sousa's marches, and like, the March of the Director. (sings) Da da da da da da da da da da da da da da da da da da da.

That was the alto horn. And the bass would go -- (sings) But, so, and then the right hand was playing the melody. And these things happened so that we got so that we could master those things pretty good. And the next thing, we had time. Because a lot of times, there was no drums with you. And if there was drums, they couldn't afford drums, because the houses and the walls was too thin, and first thing you'd know, somebody else would be complaining about the drums. And so, if you had drums, you wouldn't last much -- long. So, we went on. We passed on.
